title: Dedicated capacity onboarding orchestration & SLA negotiation ladder for enterprise hybrid workloads
creator: Arielle Chen
description:
Problem: Enterprise customers often arrive with incomplete workload profiles and strict compliance requirements. Sales and Solutions Engineering need a predictable, repeatable way to negotiate SLA targets, recommend reserved throughput, and map customers to GPU classes and scaling behaviors that match risk tolerance and cost expectations.

Goal: Create an orchestration checklist and negotiation ladder that the sales/SE/PM onboarding triage team can use to: (1) evaluate incoming requests consistently, (2) propose defensible SLA targets (p99 latency, throughput units), (3) map to recommended GPU families and fallback options, and (4) prescribe scaling and preemption policies for mixed reserved/burst patterns. The artifact should be actionable in a meeting, produce a one-page commitment summary for legal, and feed decisions into the Dedicated provisioning flow.
acceptance_criteria: A step-by-step checklist that intake leads can follow in a 30-minute customer call

A clear negotiation ladder with recommended p99/p95 targets, reservation tiers (X tokens/s or equivalent throughput units), and GPU family mappings for common workload archetypes (chat, embed-heavy, rerank, batch infer)
Decision points that account for data residency, private deployment constraints, and KMS/HSM requirements
Template commitment summary (one page) that Legal/RevOps can accept as the seed for a Reserved Capacity contract
Integration points defined for upstream: onboarding form fields in Gainsight/CRM and downstream: provisioner API and dedicated-console flags
scoring_rubric: Workload fingerprint score (0-10): based on request rate, token distribution, and burstiness (weight 30%)
Reliability demand score (0-10): compliance, SLA penalty tolerance, and multi-region requirements (weight 25%)
Cost sensitivity (0-10): willingness to pay for reserved vs burstable capacity (weight 20%)
Operational maturity (0-10): ability to provide perf tests and synthetic traces (weight 15%)
Integration friction (0-10): VPC/Private control plane, KMS integration, on-prem network constraints (weight 10%)
intake_template_questions: Peak concurrent requests and expected sustained tokens/sec (30/1h and 24h avg)
Typical request types (chat, single-shot generation, embeddings, rerank) and example prompts
Latency SLO target (p50/p95/p99) and max acceptable cold-start duration
Data residency / VPC / on-prem needs and KMS/HSM requirements
Acceptance criteria for fallback behaviour (e.g., downgrade to quantized model, regional fallback, or queued requests)
Preferred GPU families or hard exclusions (e.g., must be A100, cannot use T4)
Expected growth curve and seasonal burst patterns (dates/percentiles)
Existing latency/cost benchmarks or third-party SLOs to align against
negotiation_ladder_examples: Conservative enterprise (regulated): p99 < 120ms, reserved throughput to cover 95% of peak, GPU family: A100; preemption: none; fallback: regional warm standby with reduced model variant

Balanced SaaS (PLG with enterprise customers): p99 < 250ms, reserved covers baseline 60% of peak with burst credits for spikes, GPU family: H100 or A100 depending on cost; preemption: allowed for non-critical lanes; fallback: quantized variant with same model version

Cost-sensitive high-volume: p95 < 350ms, reserved minimal baseline (25%), aggressive burst credits, GPU family: B100/T4 equivalent; preemption: allowed; fallback: degrade to lower-context model and queue less-critical requests
